Stadiums are the cathedrals of sport — concrete memory banks where generations experienced the same joys and heartbreaks. This database covers the ground's history, architecture, great events, and how to visit it.

title: History
d: Madison Square Garden opened in 1968. The World's Most Famous Arena..
definition: Madison Square Garden opened in 1968. The World's Most Famous Arena..
description: The history of Madison Square Garden begins in 1968. The World's Most Famous Arena. Like all great grounds, it has been rebuilt, renamed, and reborn — stands rising where terraces stood, roofs arriving decades after the first kick. Its timeline is the timeline of its tenants' triumphs and the city's love affair with the game.

title: Architecture
d: Madison Square Garden holds about 20,789 spectators in its current configuration.

description: The architecture of Madison Square Garden: a 20,789-capacity bowl designed to trap noise and frame the action. Great stadium design balances sightlines, acoustics, and atmosphere — the steepest stands feel closest, the roofs hold the roar in. Renovations keep adding hospitality while trying not to dilute the soul.

title: The tenants
d: Madison Square Garden is home to Knicks, Rangers.
definition: Madison Square Garden is home to Knicks, Rangers.
description: Madison Square Garden belongs to Knicks, Rangers — and to the fans who fill it. The tenant-club bond defines the ground's identity: the songs, the rituals, the expectation. When the team thrives the stadium shakes; when it struggles the old ground groans with it. You cannot separate the venue from its people.

title: Great matches
d: The greatest nights at Madison Square Garden live in legend.
definition: The greatest nights at Madison Square Garden live in legend.
description: The great nights at Madison Square Garden: title deciders, cup finals, impossible comebacks — the matches fans describe decades later as if they were yesterday. The World's Most Famous Arena. Every old ground has a canon of such nights, and they are why the place matters: the stadium is the stage, but the drama is the point.

title: Finals hosted

definition: Madison Square Garden has hosted major finals and showpiece events.
description: Showpiece events at Madison Square Garden: cup finals, international tournaments, and one-off spectacles that put the ground on the world stage. Hosting a final is a civic honor — the city dresses up, the world watches, and the stadium joins the short list of venues that have seen it all.

title: Concerts and events
d: Madison Square Garden doubles as a concert and event venue.
definition: Madison Square Garden doubles as a concert and event venue.
description: Beyond sport, Madison Square Garden hosts concerts, ceremonies, and mega-events — the biggest stages need the biggest rooms. The ground's event history reads like pop culture itself. Multi-use keeps the economics working, though purists always prefer the roar of a matchday to anything else.

title: Visiting guide

definition: Visit Madison Square Garden: tours, matchdays, and practical tips.
description: Visiting Madison Square Garden: stadium tours run most days, taking in the dressing rooms, the tunnel, and the dugout — book ahead in season. On matchdays arrive early, learn the songs, and respect the home ends. New York, USA is best reached by public transport; driving on event days is for the patient.

title: Best seats

description: Seats at Madison Square Garden: behind the goal for the songs, halfway up the side for the tactical view, high corners for value. The famous ends have waiting lists measured in years; the family sections trade noise for comfort. Wherever you sit, the rule is the same — arrive early, stay late.

d: Madison Square Garden's biggest crowds and what drew them.
definition: Madison Square Garden's biggest crowds and what drew them.
description: The biggest crowds at Madison Square Garden came for the biggest occasions — derbies, finals, and farewell games. The World's Most Famous Arena. Capacity has changed with all-seater conversions and expansions, so records from different eras are not directly comparable. What endures is the noise: full houses here are famously loud.

title: Fan culture

definition: The songs and rituals of Madison Square Garden.

definition: Derby days at Madison Square Garden are the season's peak.

title: The future

definition: What is next for Madison Square Garden.
